operational-example.copy: Use Code Input to capture one bounded verification code without owning the full authentication journey.

scenario.title: Driver verification

items.label: OTP
items.helper: Use the code from your authenticator app.

rationale: SMS and OTP are variants of the same Code Input family: one visible code entry with channel-specific helper copy.
Code Input keeps one code entry accessible and paste-friendly.
Passcode Keypad is not a Code Input variant; it belongs to authentication patterns because it owns keypad, progress dots, biometric, and backspace behavior.
Use a pattern when code entry is combined with password, biometrics, resend policy, retry limits, or risk handling.

items.rule: Names the verification code purpose in visible text.
Show digit progress while behaving as one logical input.
Carries expiry, resend, or recovery guidance.
Makes the active slot visible for keyboard users.
Confirms code entry without submitting unrelated flows.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, error, warning, complete, focus, hover, default
items: Expose the code as one grouped input, not six unrelated fields.
Support paste and one-time-code autocomplete where the platform allows it.
Associate helper, timer, and error text with the field.
Keep slot targets large enough for touch.
Provide text-backed warning and error states.

variants.copy: Code Input variants describe code source and sensitivity while preserving one grouped code-entry contract. Use length for digit count; use variant for meaning such as sms, otp, approval, masked, or compact.

states.copy: Code Input states communicate focus, completion, expiry, error, and disabled behavior without taking over the auth pattern.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines slot treatment; state defines verification feedback while auth sequencing stays in patterns.

full-width.copy: Code Input can fill auth forms and mobile sheets while each slot keeps a minimum readable target.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Keep code slots in one readable row when possible and preserve paste/autofill behavior before changing layout.

viewport-organization.copy: Code Input should stay close to its instruction, timer, and resend action; the surrounding auth pattern owns the sequence.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use large slots and visible timer copy.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep helper copy in the same field group.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact slots inside the login column.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify code length, helper copy, variant, and state before composing an auth pattern.

api-foundations.copy: Code Input API exposes label, value, length, variant, state, and helper copy while reusing Input label/helper rhythm and owning grouped slot geometry. Passcode Keypad behavior is outside this API and belongs to authentication patterns.

props.name: length
props.notes: Number of code digits; use this instead of creating digit-count variants.

props.name: variant
props.notes: Semantic treatment for code source or sensitivity while preserving one logical input.

props.name: masked
props.notes: Masks visible slot digits while keeping the underlying one-time-code input value.

props.name: density
props.notes: Maps to shared Input rhythm for label, helper, and slot size.

props.name: error
props.notes: Error helper text; sets aria-invalid on code slots.

props.name: onComplete
props.notes: Called when all digits are filled.

groups.title: Use
items: Keep expiry and recovery copy visible.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not design the whole auth system inside Code Input.
Do not split screen readers across fake fields.

rejectIf: The code has no visible label.
Each slot is an unrelated input.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Code Input as one code-entry component. Agents may place it when a verification code is known, but humans confirm delivery channel, resend policy, expiry, and auth pattern context.
canDecide: Use Code Input for one SMS, OTP, email, or approval code.
Use length when the product code is intentionally short or long.
Use warning for expiring or resend-sensitive states.
mustAsk: The code affects money, access, or safety.
Delivery channel, expiry, or resend policy is unclear.
OTP combines with password, biometric, or risk recovery.
rejectIf: Code Input owns the whole auth system.
The code field has no label.
miel.handoff: I am using Code Input for one verification code. Please confirm channel, length, expiry, resend behavior, accessible helper text, and the surrounding auth pattern.
